newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden finance sector could handle euro -Riksbank.
newsitem.headline: Sweden finance sector could handle euro -Riksbank.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday it believed the country's financial sector could handle changing over to a common European currency from January 1999.
"The Riksbank considers that the financial sector can manager a change over to the euro on January 1, 1999," the Riksbank said in a statement.

"Participation from a later date may facilitate the preparatory work in some respects and complicate it in others. The worst alternative is a long period of uncertainty that would entail a costly duplication of systems in a number of fields."
The bank said this was the conclusion of a new report on necessary preparations if the euro is introduced in Sweden.
The Riksbank said the purpose of the report was the describe the consequences of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) on Sweden's financial sector, regardless of whether Sweden decides to join.
It said the report showed that if Sweden decided to join EMU, major Swedish players favoured a quick changeover.

"In the event of participation in EMU, the agents in the Swedish securities market -- banks, financial institutions, the Securities Register Centre, the Stockholm Stock Exchange, OM and others -- unanimously favour a 'big bang' solution, that is a prompt and complete changeover from crown to euro at the turn of 1998," it said.
It said there would be major changes even if Sweden decided not to join.
"Remaining outside EMU does not amount to status quo. However, it is up to each and every agent to decide whether and, if so, to what extent to make preparations for the single currency," it said.
